- Overestimate prices after recent spikes; model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward quickly.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or shows strong downward momentum; model reacts too slowly to bearish signals.
- Overreact to short-term sentiment swings; model often follows sentiment too closely, leading to overcorrection or undercorrection.
- Mean reversion bias: model frequently forecasts prices to revert to historical averages too aggressively, especially when sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish.
- Lag in response to sentiment shifts: model delays adjusting forecasts when sentiment turns negative, leading to persistent overestimation.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts consistently overestimate early in the period (first 5–7 days) and underestimate later, especially after a spike.
- When sentiment is high and prices are rising, model tends to overforecast the peak; when sentiment turns negative, model undercorrects and fails to anticipate sharp drops.
